subject: nereid-framing
q: CLOSED — OPULENT IS TORSO FAVORING, VOLTAIC IS EVENLY SPLIT, AND THE VALKYRIE READING WAS RIGHT.
detail:
ANSWERED, AND THE REFUSAL TO DEDUCE WAS WORTH IT TWICE OVER.

OPULENT IS TORSO FAVORING — SLIGHTLY MORE HEIGHT AND STRUCTURAL DEPTH TO THE TORSO. VOLTAIC IS EVENLY SPLIT — EVENLY DIVIDED BUT COMPACTLY ORGANISED AROUND THE JOINTS AND WORKING AXIS.

NEITHER WAS DERIVABLE FROM WHAT THE ARCHIVE HAD. PLUSHER, MORE SOFT and LITHE AND SPRY BUT KEEPS HER CURVES describe tissue and motion, not allocation, and a plush woman can be leggy while a lithe woman can be long in the torso. THE ARCHIVE SAID SO AND LEFT BOTH CELLS EMPTY.

AND THE VALKYRIE HALF-FLAG CAME BACK CONFIRMED: TORSO FAVORING, as the Archive had read it and labelled a reading. Which is q-plump-roster’s lesson arriving a second time in one session — FLAGGING AN INVENTION DOES NOT MAKE IT WRONG, AND BEING RIGHT IS NOT A REASON TO HAVE FILED IT UNFLAGGED. THE FLAG IS WHAT MADE IT SAFE TO BE RIGHT.

THE SMALLER NOTE IN THIS QUESTION IS NOW ANSWERED TOO, BY IMPLICATION: Framing travels to SILKEN EMBRACE as a DERIVED value, the only computed entry on a handoff list otherwise made of selections and measurements. The boutique receives it; nobody chose it.

AND THE QUESTION MISSED TWO ERRORS WHILE CORRECTLY CATCHING ITS OWN TWO GAPS: HUNTRESS AND DANCER were both filed wrong and NOT flagged, because a first pass had given them in ratio language and the Archive believed it. See c-framing-table. A FLAG PROTECTS THE CELL IT IS ON AND NOTHING ELSE.
